CONCIO XXV.
Proverb. 12.

l.i: Mulier sedula corona est mariti sui:
sed quasi putredo in ossibus eius est

main_text.l: 1 Hoc unum est ex dictis Salomonis,
quæ parabolæ & proverbia nuncupantur.
Parabolæ quidem sive similitudines, quia oc-
culta sunt, & secreta mysteria significat: Pro-
verbia autem, quia talia sunt, quæ sæpius in
ore fidelium versari, ac memoriæ commen-
dari, ac retineri debent. Simus igitur &
illius dicti memores, & sciamus id non solum
juxta literam esse intelligendum, sed aliter
quoque ac spiritualiter.
2 Quæ est ergo sententia simplex huius
loci? Mulierem magnum bonum, item ma-
gnum malum esse, quemadmodum etiam
Chrysostomus testatur in epistola ad Hebr.

page.notes: Top line is a fragment: "mne" begins at the left edge, so the first letter is cut off by the scan. Printed "munedi" at the line break appears to be "mundi" with the hyphen lost; marked as read. "s" and "f" are normalised to s. Small reference marks in the right and left margins beside "Amen." and the sermon heading carry no printed text, so none are transcribed as notes. The "2" of the second paragraph and the "1" of the first are printed numbers, kept as printed. "vbi" at the foot is the catchword, not part of the text.
